body: SEC-1 defines **org-scoped** signing/verification key management required for offline-capable ticket admission.
It provides **key epochs**, **key states**, and a deterministic **public key distribution** model so SCAN-1 can verify TKT-1 credentials without interpretation drift.
sections.title: Overview

body: **SEC-1-INV-001 (Org scope):** All keys, epochs, and distributions MUST be scoped by `org_id`.
**SEC-1-INV-002 (Private keys never leave secure boundary):** Private keys MUST NOT be stored in general application databases or emitted in any API; they MUST reside in an HSM/KMS or equivalent.
**SEC-1-INV-003 (Deterministic verification):** Verifiers MUST be able to verify credentials using `kid` + published public keys without online lookups.
**SEC-1-INV-004 (Rotation safety):** Routine rotation MUST NOT invalidate valid credentials during the event lifecycle; grace keys MUST be supported.
**SEC-1-INV-005 (Compromise response):** Compromise MUST be treated differently from routine rotation and MUST support forced reissue and revocation of affected keys.
**SEC-1-INV-006 (Append-only audit):** Key lifecycle events MUST be append-only and auditable.
sections.title: Invariants

body: SEC-1 defines a monotonic `key_epoch` per org and key purpose. A change that affects verifiers MUST advance the epoch.
Epoch changes MUST be represented as append-only events and MUST be reproducible from the event log.

entities.name: KeyEpoch
rules: A new epoch MUST be created on (a) routine rotation cutover, (b) compromise response, or (c) verifier policy change that affects acceptance.
An epoch MUST NOT decrease or be reused.

sections.title: Key epoch model

body: Keys for a given purpose MUST be in exactly one state: `active`, `grace`, or `revoked`.
`active` keys MAY sign and MUST verify. `grace` keys MUST verify and MUST NOT sign. `revoked` keys MUST NOT verify and MUST NOT sign.

fields.name: public_key
fields.text: The Ed25519 public key encoded as Base64URL (RFC 4648) without padding.

entities.name: PublicKey
rules: A key MUST NOT transition from `revoked` to any other state.
A key in `grace` state MUST have been previously `active` for the same purpose.

sections.title: Key states

body: SEC-1 defines a deterministic distribution payload for verifiers. The payload MUST be signed and versioned.
SCAN-1 hydration MUST consume SEC-1 distributions and MUST enforce max age bounds per EVT-2 scan policy.

entities.name: KeyDistributionSnapshot
rules: The snapshot MUST be signed using `hydration_snapshot_signing` keys (separate from ticket signing).
The snapshot MUST NOT include private key material.

sections.title: Public key distribution

body: Compromise response MUST revoke the compromised `kid` immediately and advance epoch.
Affected credentials MUST be reissued and prior credentials MUST be revoked/superseded (see TKT-1).
rules: Compromise response MUST be an explicit admin/security authority path; automated authorities MUST NOT declare compromise without an audited override.

summary: Defines key epochs, key states, and distribution semantics for offline-capable credential verification.

summary_detail.one_liner: Defines the hard boundary between the core payments domain and external PSP providers (Stripe/Paystack/PayFast/etc), including idempotency, webhook safety, tenancy isolation, and ledger separation.
summary_detail.problem: Payments integrations fail in the denial paths: duplicate webhooks, replay attacks, cross-tenant routing mistakes, and accidental ledger coupling. Without a strict adapter contract, every PSP integration invents its own semantics.
summary_detail.solution: A single PSP adapter interface with mandatory security, idempotency, and tenancy invariants; all PSP input is normalized into core domain resources/events; the adapter may never mutate core tables directly nor decide ledger postings. Additionally: webhook ingestion is state-aware and replay-safe; 2xx acknowledgement requires durable ingest plus guaranteed enqueue/sweeper recovery.

inspect_maintenance_requirements.description: CI fails if new field added to payment structs without Inspect exclusion.

title: Security Keys & Epochs

anti_patterns: Performing heavy work synchronously inside webhook handler before persisting to durable storage/queue.
Using 'ticket lookup' or 'transaction lookup' endpoints that allow enumeration of valid IDs.
Routing tenant by untrusted URL params without signature-bound metadata.
Treating 'HTTP 2xx returned' as proof that downstream processing completed.
Rejecting replayed webhook deliveries solely because (provider, provider_account_ref, provider_event_id) exists, without checking processing_state and requeueing when non-terminal.

processing_model.ack_2xx_rule: MUST durably ingest ProviderEvent and (enqueue processing job OR ensure sweeper will enqueue within stale windows) before returning any 2xx response.

processing_job_semantics.idempotency_rule: Job MUST be safe to run multiple times; side-effects MUST be fenced by idempotency keys and/or optimistic updates on target resources.

requeue_rules: If processing_state=='received' and age_seconds > received_stale_after_seconds: enqueue job and set state='queued'.
If processing_state=='processing' and age_seconds > processing_stale_after_seconds: enqueue job and set state='queued' (stuck steal).
If processing_state in ['failed','dead_letter']: allow manual replay by requeueing existing row (no new row).

dedupe_strategy.on_conflict: MUST load existing ProviderEvent row and act by processing_state

approved_authority_corrections.identity_security_boundary: Authentication MUST resolve through a trusted provider to global AuthIdentity keyed by exact (issuer, provider_subject). Email equality MUST NOT merge principals. IAM MUST NOT access PII-1 subject_lookup_key_hash.
